edges.rationale: Queuing delay is one of the four nodal delay components introduced here; the deep-dive on dqueue presupposes the dnodal = dproc + dqueue + dtrans + dprop framework and the notion of a router queue.
End-to-end delay is defined as the accumulation of nodal delays along the path, so the nodal delay components and formula must be understood first.
Packet loss is explained via finite queue capacity and is explicitly related to traffic intensity La/R approaching or exceeding 1, a quantity defined in the queuing-delay discussion.

The bottleneck-link model and the file-transfer-time approximation F/min{Rs, Rc} rely on the transmission-rate/transmission-delay concept, and its stated caveats (ignoring store-and-forward and processing delays) require knowing those nodal delay components.
